# FDGD054

> NOT PERMITTED: Changing the Default Value for an Optional Parameter

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section D.11.18 Changing the Default Value for an Optional Parameter. Can cause: recompile break.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library warning, application none, test none
- Status: draft

Callers keep the old default until they recompile, so the compiled binary and the source disagree. PublicApiAnalyzers (optional in /fdg-setup) can flag changes to the public API.

## From the book

Optional parameters are a compile-time feature in which any caller that did not provide a value for a parameter gets the value from the target member’s metadata. Changing the default value has no effect on callers until they recompile, which can create confusion where the compiled binary and the developer’s understanding of the program from the source code do not match.

The .NET BCL team considers this an unacceptable breaking change due to the possibility of developer confusion.
